summary: The Assemblies of God's Statement of Fundamental Truths, as summarized in an AG lesson that reproduces it, teaches that humanity's only hope of redemption is the shed blood of Jesus Christ. A person receives salvation by acknowledging sin, repenting toward God and declaring faith in the Lord Jesus Christ as Savior. By this a person stands justified before God by his grace and may experience spiritual renewal, or regeneration, by the Holy Spirit, and so becomes an heir of God with the hope of eternal life. The statement names two evidences of salvation: the inward witness of the Spirit and the outward evidence of a life pursuing righteousness and holiness. The wording read does not address election or whether a believer can fall away.

points.question: How is a person saved?
points.answer: By acknowledging sin, repenting toward God and declaring faith in the Lord Jesus Christ as Savior; through this a person stands justified before God by his grace and may be regenerated by the Holy Spirit.

review.note: Written from the first paragraph of an AG men's ministry lesson that quotes the statement, read on 2026-11-12, and a search result showing the official wording; the official ag.org text could not be fetched, so the exact wording is unchecked.
